extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, organizations, and stakeholders submitting public comments to EPA dockets via Regulations.gov or other accepted channels
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments to EPA dockets (preferred via Regulations.gov), including content, formatting, procedural, confidentiality, and posting rules to maximize the likelihood that comments will be considered and used in agency decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations.gov is our preferred method of receiving comments. However, other submission formats are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a complete list of all accepted types and relevant mailing addresses, visit 'Where to Send Comments'. Use Regulations.gov when possible to ensure consistent processing and public posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify docket and identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the docket ID number and other identifying information (e.g., subject heading, Federal Register date and page number) in your subject line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments cannot be considered if they are misdirected or get lost because the identifying information was not included. Include docket ID, subject heading, FR date/page as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and understand the document
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and understand the document you are commenting on; if you have difficulty understanding it, reach out to the EPA contact person named in the document and describe that difficulty in your comments along with the clarification you received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you sought clarification from the EPA contact, explain the nature of your difficulty and summarize the response so reviewers understand your interpretation or remaining concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow directions and cite regulatory references
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow directions provided by the agency; the Agency may ask you to respond to specific questions, provide particular information or organize comments in a particular way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If commenting on a proposed regulatory provision, include the reference to the proposed part and section number for the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR). Organize responses as the agency requests to facilitate processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be concise but support your claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Be concise but support your claims. Explain your views clearly and avoid profanity or personal threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why you agree or disagree; suggest alternatives and substitute language for your requested changes. Provide specific examples to illustrate concerns. Avoid profanity/threats (these will be rejected).

rubrics_metrics.name: Base comments on sound reasoning and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Base your comments on sound reasoning, scientific evidence, and/or how you will be impacted by the agency’s proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe any assumptions and provide the technical information and/or data used. If you estimate potential costs or burdens, explain how you arrived at your estimate in sufficient detail to allow it to be reproduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address trade-offs and opposing views
rubrics_metrics.description: Address trade-offs and opposing views in your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss counterarguments and why your proposed alternative or position better balances policy goals, costs, benefits, or other considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality over quantity (not a vote)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment process is not a vote – one well‑supported comment is often more informative to the agency than a thousand form letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize substantive, evidence-backed comments rather than mass form letters to increase the likelihood your points are considered in decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet the comment period deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure to submit your comments by the comment period deadline identified in the Federal Register document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late comments may not be considered. Verify the deadline in the Federal Register notice for each rulemaking or docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: No threatening language or profanity
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments containing threatening language or profanity will be rejected without notice from the EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use professional, non-threatening language. Profanity or threats can result in immediate rejection and non-posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia submissions must include written comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written comment; the written comment is considered the official comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include discussion of all points you wish to make in the written portion; do not rely on audio/video alone as they are secondary to the written submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on content located outside the primary submission
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all substantive content within the submitted comment or attachments in the primary submission; references to external links are not a substitute for including the material directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of copyrighted material
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclusion of any copyrighted material without accompanying proof of one's explicit right to redistribute that material will result in the comment being blocked from online viewing at Regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including copyrighted content, provide proof of redistribution rights or avoid including it. Materials without proof may be blocked from online display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) and restricted disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute should never be sent to EPA electronically via Regulations.gov or e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you wish to include CBI, clearly mark the part or all of the information that you claim to be CBI. Submit one complete version that includes CBI and also a non-CBI copy for the public docket. For TSCA CBI claims, follow additional TSCA-specific requirements (see 40 CFR Part 703) and use EPA’s CDX/TSCA General Communications Tool. Contact the EPA Docket Center or Docket Customer Service for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark other statutorily restricted information
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish to include other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute in your comment, clearly mark your submission as including that information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information so marked will be processed by the EPA Docket Center in accordance with the applicable statute; contact the docket center for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass mail campaign and bundled submission posting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In instances where individual submissions are duplicate or near-duplicate copies as part of a mass mail campaign, EPA will post one representative sample comment along with the total comment count for that campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submissions are bundled together (submitted as a single document or packaged together), EPA will post all comments along with the total comment count; this includes hardcopy-handwritten bundled campaigns that are scanned into PDFs. The exception: a bundled campaign of hardcopy form letters/form postcards — EPA will post one representative sample plus the total count. See the Submission Type Posting Overview for details by web/email/hardcopy and individual vs. mass campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized comment form data fields (Beta Regulations.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Beta Regulations.gov comment form (standardized as of Feb 19, 2021) uses standardized data fields for all agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key Beta form fields: Type of Commenter (Individual/Organization/Anonymous); Comment (Required); Email Address (Optional); First Name (Required for Individuals); Last Name (Required for Individuals); City/State/Zip/Country/Phone/Attach Files (Optional or N/A depending on commenter type); Organization Type/Organization Name required for organizations. Refer to the page's Table 1 for the full field mapping and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classic comment form data fields (pre-June 4, 2019) for EPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to June 4, 2019 EPA used the Classic Regulations.gov comment form with a different set of available fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classic EPA form fields included Comment (Required) and various name/address/contact fields that were N/A on the Beta form; Upload Files was Optional; Submitter's Representative and Organization Name were Optional. See the page's Table 2 for the full Classic form field mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and access to comment data
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments submitted to EPA (including any personal information in the body) will be posted to Regulations.gov and are also available for in-person viewing at the EPA Docket Center’s Reading Room, with exceptions noted in Rules and Restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations.gov provides public access via the web interface, bulk comment data download, and an API. For documentation on which collected data fields are made available to data users, contact the GSA Regulations.gov helpdesk or Regulations.gov Support.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA use of artificial intelligence in comment processing
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain rulemakings and actions, EPA may use artificial intelligence to help sort and categorize public comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI use is intended to identify substantive comments, separate topical arguments, and sort key points by theme for human reviewers; AI may also generate individual comment summaries to aid processing. Human supervision and input remain required throughout comment processing; the basis for agency responses remains the comments themselves and responses are drafted by humans. Quality assurance occurs to ensure comprehensive review.
